page: Amazon Web Services m8i.96xlarge is a large-scale general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz across 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system features a large cache subsystem with 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity totals 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, providing a standard general purpose memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration is supported through AVX-512 extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, while no local instance storage is bundled, requiring the use of external network-attached block volumes.

Benchmark testing reflects exceptional multi-threaded computational and throughput capabilities. In multi-core CPU benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng with 414,725.92 points, PassMark CPU tests at 177,699.21 points, and software compilation tasks reaching 64,262.0 points. Cached read memory bandwidth measures at 30,541.88 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read bandwidth reaches 1,145.17 GB/sec. Data processing capability is highlighted by Redis performance reaching 508.55 million SET operations per second and static web throughput of 220.49 GB/sec. Parallel decompression via bzip3 also demonstrates top-tier output at 1,837.08 GB/sec, alongside strong single-core Geekbench and compression metrics.

The primary tradeoff of the instance centers on its CPU-only architecture and reliance on external storage. Lacking discrete GPUs, generative text decoding throughput remains modest, scoring in the lower percentiles on small model token generation compared to dedicated accelerators. However, its substantial vCPU count, wide memory bandwidth, and 100 Gbps networking deliver solid resource density for non-GPU enterprise workloads. The hardware profile fits distributed caching clusters, large-scale Redis deployments, CI/CD compilation farms, parallel batch processing, enterprise databases, and high-throughput web serving environments.
